output.summary: KEP-1498 proposed extending the patch-fix support window for each Kubernetes minor release from about 9 months to about 14 months (12 months support plus 2 months upgrade period). Its status is recorded as implemented, stage stable, from 2021-01-15.
output.rationale: Users needed annual support cycles to match business planning, and a survey showed about a third of production users were on versions out of the 9-month window. The KEP proposed a 14-month cadence, formalizing the existing practice of keeping patch branch CI about 6-7 weeks beyond the 9-month phase. The status-related discussion in the sources concerns the KEP's status metadata and PRR process, not the support-policy substance.

alternatives.option: No change to the 9-month support window
alternatives.why_not: The readme says this 'continue[s] to leave users unsatisfied' and that many users fail to upgrade within 9 months.

alternatives.option: Longer support period of 2, 3, or 5 years
alternatives.why_not: The readme says this is 'hard to implement in the current context of the project's practices' and that all the work in the KEP would be required anyway first.

alternatives.option: Change the release cadence to produce more stable releases
alternatives.why_not: The readme calls this 'orthogonal' and notes it 'may also do the opposite' for supportability.

alternatives.option: Tim St. Clair's devel/stable split proposal, or Lubomir Ivanov's 18-month LTS proposal
alternatives.why_not: The readme says both 'may be compatible and complementary with the change proposed in this KEP' and are possible future changes rather than alternatives to this one.

evidence.quote: The goal of this KEP is to increase patch-fix support for each Kubernetes release from the current 9 months to 1 year.
The proposal is to extend the Kubernetes support cadence from 9 months to 14 months. The 14 months proposed here is essentially 12 months of support and 2 months of upgrade period.
The survey conducted in early 2019 by the WG LTS showed that a significant subset of Kubernetes end-users fail to upgrade within the 9-month support period.
This KEP was initially declared implementable at alpha, before PRR was required. The retroactive PR incorrectly called this "implemented" at beta, so it skipped PRR this cycle.
